summary: Opaque 5xx elevation during mixed embedding uploads and short streaming chat; proxy FD throttle observed
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Acme AI) reported a sudden ~8-12 minute spike of 502/503 responses across a subset of eu-west host pools during a mixed workload: large embedding bulk uploads interleaved with many short-lived streaming chat sessions. The spike coincided with elevated proxy file-descriptor throttle metrics and a jump in runtime restart events.

Impact:
- Multiple production endpoints returned 5xxs for ~8-12 minutes for the customer tenant; increased token failure rate ~18% for that window.
- Short-lived streams (chat) saw connection resets and aborted streaming frames.
- Embedded bulk uploads saw elevated first-byte timeouts and retries, causing backoff amplifications.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted, customer assigned Dedicated pool in eu-west.
- Affected instances: ephemeral-proxy fleet nodes (eu-west-a/b), serving-runtime shards pinned to dedicated GPUs.
- Time window: 2026-03-13T18:02:00Z — 2026-03-13T18:14:00Z.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Customer starts a bulk embedding upload (multipart, ~3000 small items in parallel) to embedding route.
2) Simultaneously dozens of short streaming chat sessions are opened by web clients (many short-lived: connect -> prompt -> disconnect).
3) Proxy accept queue grows; ephemeral-proxy FD throttle metric increments; some proxy instances start returning 502 to api-gateway.
4) Serving runtime shows prefetch/kvcache worker stalls, and selective runtimes restart (OOM watchdog sometimes triggered after stall).

Observed logs/metrics (snips):
- proxy-fd-throttle: surge from 0.02 -> 0.48 across nodes
- apigw.error_rate[eu-west]: 4.7% -> 22.1% during window
- runtime.restart_count: +7 in 12m on shard-57

Logs (excerpt):
"2026-03-13T18:04:21Z proxy[eu-west-a] WARN accept_queue_full fd_throttle=0.41 backlog=312"
"2026-03-13T18:05:03Z runtime[shard-57] ERROR kvcache_worker hung for 120s; stacktrace attached"
"2026-03-13T18:05:07Z apigw[eu-west] ERROR upstream_connect failed: connection_reset by peer"

Initial mitigation taken:
- Support applied a transient rate-limit on the customer's embedding upload route (reduced concurrent multipart parts to 8) and instructed client to retry with exponential backoff.
- Redirected a portion of tenant traffic to warm standby hosts in eu-west-b.
- Pager alerted SRE and on-call runtime engineer to trace kvcache thread hangs.

Next steps (high level):
- SRE to capture full runtime core dump and profiling traces from shard-57.
- Infra to run ephemeral-proxy heap and FD diagnostics, and investigate accept queue drain behavior.
- Engineering to validate kvcache worker refcount and prefetch cancellation interaction under mixed embedding+stream load.
comments: 2026-03-13 18:09 - Maya Singh (Support): Customer reported elevated 502s; triaged and escalated to SRE. Applied temporary embedding concurrency cap and suggested client-side rate limiting.
2026-03-13 18:21 - Diego Ramos (SRE): Observed FD throttle spike on 4 proxy nodes; started collecting netstat/lsof samples and epoll backlog metrics.

2026-03-13 18:33 - Claire Nguyen (Runtime Eng): Noted repeated kvcache_worker hang signatures; requested full runtime logs and core from shard-57. Hypothesis: prefetch cancellation races under high accept-queue pressure.
2026-03-13 19:02 - Acme AI (Customer): Confirmed embedding upload was triggered as part of daily sync and could stagger uploads; asked for guidance to avoid future outages.

2026-03-13 20:10 - Diego Ramos (SRE): Uploaded collected artifacts to S3: s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/SUP-1000001/ (profiles, lsof, netstat, runtime-cores). Linked PR created for temporary proxy throttle alert tuning.
investigation_notes: Collected lsof snapshots show ephemeral-proxy retaining ~1200 sockets in CLOSE_WAIT on affected hosts during peak; garbage collect loop not reclaiming quickly enough.
netstat -an on proxy nodes shows large accept backlog (tcp_accept_queue ~300) coincident with apigw retries and hedged retry amplification.

Runtime core from shard-57 indicates kvcache worker thread blocked on prefetch cancellation wait; stack points to refcount path that increments when request is accepted and decremented on close — race with socket teardown observed.
No immediate evidence of GPU OOM; runtime restarts appear secondary to watchdog timeouts triggered by blocked kvcache threads and growing event loop latencies.

Hypothesis A: Mixed workload (many short streaming connects + large multipart embed) causes ephemeral-proxy to hit FD throttle; accept queue growth causes upstream backlog and increased hedged retries, which in turn triggers duplicate prefetch attempts causing kvcache worker lock contention and a hang -> watchdog kill -> runtime restart -> 5xx wave.

Hypothesis B: A latent issue in proxy's CLOSE_WAIT cleanup under heavy multipart uploads created FD pressure; the proxy's backpressure signal isn't being propagated quickly enough to apigw causing retry storms.

Dashboards checked: apigw/accept-queue, proxy/fd-usage, runtime/kvcache-hang-count, customer/tenant-concurrency. Correlation between proxy FD usage and kvcache hang count is strong (Pearson r ~0.78 for the event window).
temporary_workarounds: Reduced customer's embedding parallelism (server-side) to 8 concurrent parts — immediate error rate dropped to baseline within 90s.
Implemented a conservative apigw backoff override for embedding endpoints for the affected tenant to avoid hedged retry amplification.
Blackholed a subset of ephemeral-proxy nodes exhibiting heavy CLOSE_WAIT until kernel reclaim completed (careful rolling to avoid capacity loss).
resolution_plan: (in-progress) Engineering will: 1) patch kvcache prefetch cancellation to avoid refcount races under early socket teardown, 2) add a short-term proxy CLOSE_WAIT scavenger to reclaim FDs faster, and 3) tune apigw hedged retry thresholds for embedding multipart endpoints. Target for PRs and canary: 2026-03-18. SRE to monitor apigw error floor and proxy FD metrics post-deploy.
follow_up_actions: Post-deploy smoke test with mixed embedding + short streaming workload to validate fix under controlled load.
Add an alert for sustained proxy CLOSE_WAIT ratio > 0.15 on any node in a pool, and a dashboard panel for kvcache prefetch hang rate per shard.
Customer-facing CC: provide recommended upload pattern (staggered multipart, lower concurrency) and incident summary when resolved.
Consider adding tenant-level admission control for embedding uploads when concurrent streaming sessions exceed a threshold.
